name: Suleviae

attributes.attribute: a Continental goddess whose name means the many Suls
Caesar tied the group to Minerva

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Suleviae is a Continental Celtic goddess. The records of her cult survive in several dozen inscriptions spread across the western lands of the Roman empire. Her name appears to mean the many Suls, so it points back to the British healing goddess Sul and binds the two worship to one current. Caesar, when he wrote of the Gauls, linked this group of goddesses with the Roman Minerva, who ruled over healing. The name takes a plural form, as if one goddess stood for a family of powers, each tied to the same warm spring and the same act of cure.
